title: Privilege Escalation
summary: A non-standard SUID binary was abused to read a sensitive file. Reconstruct what happened.
briefing:
Incident responders recovered forensic artifacts from a compromised NebulaCorp workstation. A low-privilege user account was able to read /etc/shadow — a file normally readable only by root.

The responders collected:
- The output of find / -perm -4000 (SUID binaries)
- The user's recovered bash history
- Relevant syslog entries
- Directory listing and file details for a suspicious binary

Analyze these artifacts to determine:
1. Which SUID binary does NOT belong to the standard OS installation?
2. What sensitive file was read through it?
3. Which user account exploited it?

Submit: RANGE{suid_<binary_name>_<sensitive_file_basename>_<username>}

For example, if the binary were /opt/tools/helper, the file /etc/passwd, and the user admin1: RANGE{suid_helper_passwd_admin1}
objectives: Identify the non-standard SUID binary from the find output
Trace how it was used in the bash history
Confirm the sensitive file access in syslog

hints.title: Standard vs custom
hints.text: Standard SUID binaries live in /usr/bin/ and /usr/lib/. Look for one in an unusual location like /opt/.

hints.title: Trace the attack
hints.text: The binary is /opt/nebula/logmon. The bash history shows it was used with --read /etc/shadow. The user is dev01.

artifacts.description: Output of find / -perm -4000 on the compromised host.
Recovered bash history for the suspect user.
Syslog entries around the incident window.
File details for the suspicious binary.
